title: Matching words with photos and listening about speeding and crime scene evidence
summary: The page begins with a vocabulary matching activity pairing words with photos, followed by a listening task with two speakers: one recounts a past speeding experience and its consequences, while the other describes how police find and analyse fingerprints and footprints at a crime scene.

title: Completing sentences with past and past-continuous tenses, plus a timelines study tip
summary: An exercise asks learners to fill gaps using forms such as used to, was walking and were speeding to distinguish finished habits, specific past actions and simultaneous actions. A study tip then introduces timelines as a tool for choosing the right tense, with an example to copy.

title: Vocabulary, comprehension and listening exercises about a police officer's duties
summary: Learners find vocabulary in texts about police work, complete sentences about traffic control and crime-scene evidence, answer comprehension questions, and listen to an audio clip about the dangers, hours and rewards of being a police officer.

title: Exercises on must, mustn't, have to, needn't and need to for rules and obligations
summary: The first task requires learners to extract phrases with must, have to, needn't and similar forms from a text, then classify which modal expressions state necessity, prohibition or optionality. A second exercise applies all six forms to complete sentences about driving rules, smoking restrictions and police duties.

title: Airport security vocabulary matching and reordering words to form polite questions
summary: An eight-word matching exercise covers terms such as baggage, screening, declare and unattended. Learners then rearrange jumbled words to build six questions and offers typically used at an airport, practising polite request structures.

title: Sentence gaps, identifying speech functions and choosing correct modal verbs for requests and advice
summary: Learners fill one-word gaps to create requests and suggestions, then label sentences as polite request, suggestion, advice or offer. A final exercise has them choose between two modal options in each sentence and write their own examples of the four speech functions.

title: Job advert vocabulary with abbreviations and comprehension questions about a security guard position
summary: Exercises ask learners to expand abbreviated words such as office bldgs and spk. Engl., identify abbreviations for concepts like appointment and experience, and then answer reading-comprehension questions about the personality, skills and experience required for a security-guard job.

title: Listening to a job enquiry, analysing telephone phrases, and matching sentence halves with should
summary: After completing notes from an audio conversation between a job applicant and a manager, learners select the correct alternative in six telephone exchanges, then match sentence beginnings about a new job to endings using should to express expectations.
